prompt:
I playtested it. Problems:
- The Output window shows errors:
    ServerScriptService.Server.Zombies:167: Script timeout: exhausted allowed execution time
- No zombies spawn.
- The zombies don't come toward me.
- Killing zombies doesn't give me coins or kills (the leaderboard doesn't change).
- The game never gets to wave 2.
- Zombies don't hurt me when they touch me.
- I never see the upgrade shop with offers between waves.
- I can't see a proper HUD (wave number, timer and health).
Please fix these before adding anything new.
result_text:
I found one definite bug and fixed it. I couldn't find a cause for the other symptoms. I haven't run anything, because there's no Rojo or Studio here, so please playtest.

**The fix (`src/server/Zombies.server.lua`, wave loop):** this is the cause of the `Zombies:167: Script timeout` error. When every player was dead, the loop set `gameOver`, cleared the zombies and restarted at wave 1. The next iteration saw `everyoneDead()` still true and broke out at once. That repeated forever without ever calling `task.wait`, so Roblox killed the script. After a game over, the loop now waits (checking once a second) until a player has respawned and is alive. I haven't confirmed this is what hung your playtest.

**Other symptoms:** the wave loop drives everything on your list. It spawns zombies, publishes the wave and zombie-count values the HUD reads, and opens the shop. A hung or dead wave loop could therefore explain every symptom. If so, the zombies not chasing you, hurting you, giving coins or kills, and the missing HUD and shop would all clear up with this one fix. I read the chase, contact-damage, coin and kill code, the HUD and the shop UI. I didn't see a separate bug in any of them.

I also couldn't explain why everyone would count as dead at the start of your playtest. That is the only way I can see to reach the hang so early, so the fix may not cover what you hit.

**If it still fails:** send me the full Output window from a fresh playtest, including any red errors above or below the timeout. The first error that appears will show whether something else is breaking.
